title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is preparing a 'transcendental' description of complex elliptic curves, with a view to rigidifications and moduli. On the next page he records E as the data (Π = π1(E,0), an orientation of V = Π⊗R ≅ t_E, and a point of a half-plane). On the previous page he fixed a 2-dimensional real vector space V with a complex structure c_ω. Equivalently, the circle group U = {|z|=1} acts on V; together with an orientation ω this gives the order-4 element u_ω, the rotation by +π/2. Then V_C splits into the two eigenlines L_ω (formula 14), on which U acts through the character φ_ω.

This page:
(i) It closes the bracket. The map L_ω → V, z ↦ Re z, is an isomorphism of complex vector spaces when V carries c_ω. In modern terms, V^{1,0} (the +i eigenspace of J) maps C-linearly and isomorphically onto (V,J) by the real part. Check: Re(v − iJv) = v, and Re(i(v − iJv)) = Jv.
(ii) For dim_R V = 2, complex lines in V_C are the points of Σ = Σ_V = P(C), where P = P(V) ≅ P^1_R is the projective line of V viewed as a real scheme (formula 16).
(iii) A line L defines a complex structure on V, i.e. Re: L → V is an isomorphism, iff L ∩ V = 0. This holds iff L is not the complexification of a real line L_0 ⊂ V, i.e. iff the point of L does not lie in Σ_R = P(R) (formula 17: z ∈ Σ \ Σ_R).
(iv) Conclusion, carried to the next page: complex structures on V correspond bijectively to the non-real points of P^1(C). There are two components, the upper and lower half-planes, matching the two orientations of V.

Marginal note: he hesitates whether one should attach to the complex structure L_ω or rather the other eigenline, i.e. the conjugate line. This is the usual H_1 vs H^1 / Hodge-filtration sign-convention issue.

This is the standard description of the period domain for weight-1, rank-2 Hodge structures, i.e. the Poincaré half-plane, phrased scheme-theoretically as P^1(C) minus P^1(R) for the real form P(V).
errors: No mathematical error. The convention ambiguity flagged in the margin (L_ω versus its conjugate) is real but harmless: both conventions occur in the literature, and the choice only swaps the two half-planes / orientations.

ideas.what: Complex structures J on a real 2-dimensional V correspond to the +i eigenline L ⊂ V_C with L ∩ V = 0, and Re: L → (V,J) is C-linear.
The space of complex structures on R^2 is P^1(C) \ P^1(R) for the real scheme P(V). It has two components, one for each orientation, giving the half-plane Σ_ω.
ideas.modern_name: period domain = upper ∪ lower half-plane (Siegel space for g=1)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, intrinsic, coordinate-free textbook material on complex structures and the period half-plane, written as preparation for Torelli rigidifications. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The insertion above 'rang 1' is not 'cotang 1'. It most likely reads 'complexe 1' or a similar word, i.e. 'de rang complexe 1'; the reading is uncertain.
'et l'ensemble des droites projectives réelles' is probably 'est l'espace/le schéma (des droites) projectif réel associé à V', i.e. P = P(V) is the real projective line of V.
Margin, approximately: 'Mais il y a lieu d'associer à cette structure complexe sur V non pas L_ω, mais L_ω' (ou plutôt ...)'. It concerns the choice of eigenline / conjugate convention.
'Σ(R)' in the struck/corrected phrase is written as Σ(R), then restated as Σ_R = P(R).
